clue.text: After dinner, trail all over the place with poor Podsnap

indicators.text: all over the place with poor
indicators.note: letters scattered all over the place, and a poor or mangled version of a name, both mean the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner rambles off on a rambling tangent with the pompous Mr Podsnap from Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place with poor' tells you to shuffle TRAIL and PODSNAP together. Podsnap is the smug gentleman in Dickens's Our Mutual Friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Postprandial is the Latin-derived adjective for whatever happens once a meal is finished.

clue.text: Film: Caledonian waterway

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of Caledonia, the old name for Scotland
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A documentary about a Scottish canal.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR lost the first word; the page prints 'Film'. URE is a Yorkshire river, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is an everyday word for a movie, as in 'going to the pictures'.

clue.text: She produces note on national insurance article

parts.note: so (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
NI is the standard abbreviation for National Insurance, the UK payroll contribution
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman writes a memo about her National Insurance contributions.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonia is a girl's name, so it stands for any woman referred to as she.

clue.text: Dawdling about with Beatrix or Leach in Gateshead

parts.note: Beatrix Potter wrote Peter Rabbit, and Bernard Leach was a famous studio potter
read as 'Gate's head', the first letter of the word gate

explanation.surface: Someone idles around with a children's author or a ceramicist in a town on Tyneside.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town across the Tyne from Newcastle; here it splits as 'Gate's head', giving G. Leach is a potter by trade, Beatrix one by surname.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to occupy oneself in a leisurely, aimless way, which is idling about.

clue.text: Flower Nora found wild in Italy

indicators.note: something gone wild is out of control, so these four letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman called Nora is discovered running wild on an Italian holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means something that flows, a river; 'in Italy' adds that the river is Italian, the one through Florence and Pisa.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords a flower is a river, a thing that flows, and this one flows through Tuscany.

clue.text: Act on vote for nominal change

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
a poll is a vote or ballot

explanation.surface: Legislators act on a ballot about renaming something.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' simply puts DEED above POLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed poll is the legal document a person signs in Britain to change their name officially.

clue.text: Artist accepts order sent by word of mouth

indicators.note: one word accepts another by taking it inside itself

parts.note: ARA, an Associate of the Royal Academy, is a crossword artist
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A painter receives an honour, and news of it is passed on orally.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is itself a sound-alike: 'sent' spoken is 'scent', which the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant smell, or scent, is what the word means, and 'sent' said out loud is that word.

clue.text: Preserve French artists from drug

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins
Les Nabis were a group of French post-impressionist painters including Bonnard and Vuillard

explanation.surface: Keep some French painters away from narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis is the plant-derived narcotic also called marijuana or hashish.

clue.text: One of the strings in a racket

explanation.surface: A single string is strung into a tennis racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A violin belongs to an orchestra's string section, and a dishonest scheme or scam is also called by this word.

clue.text: The Lady of the Lake?

parts.note: not the Arthurian figure: a woman's name that is also the name of a large lake on the borders of Germany, Switzerland and Austria

explanation.surface: Who is the mysterious Arthurian enchantress?
explanation.walkthrough: The Arthurian enchantress is the false trail; the 'lady' is simply a woman's name that also names the Bodensee.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name that is also the English name of the Bodensee, the lake where Germany, Switzerland and Austria meet.

clue.text: One of the Arab statesmen can be back in a minute

indicators.note: the phrase is turned round, so it is read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: 'in a mo' is informal for in a minute, mo being a moment

explanation.surface: A Gulf politician promises to return shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be back' reverses IN A MO, the colloquial 'in a moment'. 'Arab statesmen' is read as men of an Arab state.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the sultanate on the south-east of the Arabian peninsula, one of the Arab states.

clue.text: Employs silver injection in treatments

indicators.note: an injection goes into something, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: to employ something is to use it
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A doctor uses silver injections in therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Usages are customary ways of handling or treating something, so they are treatments.

clue.text: Dashed round waterfall and got a wrench

indicators.note: one word is placed round the other, holding it inside

parts.note: to dash is to hurry, so dashed is sped
rain is literally water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted around a cascade and twisted an ankle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waterfall' is not a cascade but water falling from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a sudden twisting injury to a joint, so to suffer one is to have hurt the ankle or wrist that way.

clue.text: Impose limited settlement

explanation.surface: Lay down terms for a restricted agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose is to necessitate or involve as a consequence; in law it also means a settlement restricting an estate's inheritance to a fixed line of heirs.

clue.text: Was Gay's Jemmy a fidget?

explanation.surface: Was a character in John Gay's opera a restless person?
explanation.walkthrough: Jemmy Twitcher is a highwayman in John Gay's The Beggar's Opera (1728).
explanation.definitionFit: Jemmy Twitcher is a gang member in The Beggar's Opera; one who twitches is a restless person.

clue.text: Qualified as bachelor?

explanation.surface: Did the graduate get a Bachelor's degree?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bachelor' suggests a university degree; it is the unmarried man of the stock phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fit or entitled to be chosen, and it is the stock adjective for a desirable unmarried man.

clue.text: Dope obtained with Berber support

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits underneath, so it comes second

parts.note: got means obtained
the Berbers of North Africa were classed as a Hamitic people, hence a Hamite

explanation.surface: Drugs acquired with help from North African tribesmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' is a fool, not a drug: the men of Gotham, Nottinghamshire, were famed for foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of Gotham, the English village whose people were proverbially simple-minded, so a fool.

clue.text: Under the rule of Frank, women were unsuccessful!

definitions.text: Under the rule of Frank, women were unsuccessful!

parts.words: Under the rule of Frank, women were unsuccessful!
parts.note: a Frank is one of the Germanic people of early France, whose code of rules barred women from succeeding to the throne

explanation.surface: Women did badly under an outspoken ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like candour and 'unsuccessful' like failure; really they are the Franks and inheriting the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The Frankish legal code that excluded females from inheriting land and later the French throne.

clue.text: Old Bob can get poet to fish

parts.note: a bob was slang for a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s
a can is a tin
Thomas Gray wrote Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard

explanation.surface: An elderly man named Bob persuades a poet to go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was the pre-1971 British shilling, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat ray with a venomous barbed tail, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Tone down a reminder from club secretary?

explanation.surface: Soften a letter from the club's secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is 'sub due': your subscription is due.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate or soften something; and split in two it is the notice that a membership fee is payable.

clue.text: Arrest of old Women's Land Army backed by secret service

indicators.note: backed means turned round so it reads back to front

parts.note: the ATS, Auxiliary Territorial Service, was the British women's army of the Second World War
SIS is the Secret Intelligence Service, Britain's MI6

explanation.surface: Wartime land girls are detained with backing from spies.
explanation.walkthrough: The Land Army proper was a civilian body; the setter loosely uses the women's wartime army, the ATS. 'backed' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrest here means a halt or standstill, and stasis is a state of no movement.

clue.text: Hardly a bird seen in covert!

indicators.note: one word is seen inside another

parts.note: covert means secret or sly
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Barely any birds are spotted in the thicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardly' means harshly, not barely; 'covert' is an adjective, not a thicket.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardly in its old sense of harshly or severely, as in being dealt with hardly.

clue.text: Kid stuff?

parts.note: kid is leather from a young goat, so 'kid stuff' suggests a leather; this one is made from a male deer

explanation.surface: Is it something childish?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid stuff' reads as childish things, but kid is goatskin leather and a buck is a young man as well as a male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft leather made from deer hide, and a buck is a male deer; kid, too, is a leather.

clue.text: They are taken by Partisans in the Borders

explanation.surface: Resistance fighters capture positions in southern Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Borders is a region of Scotland, but here just edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Partisans each take a position in a dispute; the edges or margins of a shape are also so called.

clue.text: Pall cast by Elijah over successor

explanation.surface: The prophet threw a shroud over his heir.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2 Kings, the prophet Elijah threw his cloak over Elisha to mark him as his successor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pall is a cloak or covering; it is also the cloak the prophet let fall on Elisha.

clue.text: Stuff introduced by Harris is on the borderline

explanation.surface: Material brought in by Harris is marginal.
explanation.walkthrough: Harris tweed is cloth woven in the Outer Hebrides; the River Tweed forms part of the England-Scotland border.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough woollen cloth, the famous Harris one; also the river along the Anglo-Scottish frontier.

clue.text: Firm way to tie up a lot of wood

explanation.surface: A secure method for bundling a heap of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong string or thin rope for binding; also a measure of stacked firewood, 128 cubic feet.

clue.text: Aim of Indian province is to raise the lowly

indicators.note: aim of the province places the aim after the province

parts.note: UP is Uttar Pradesh, a state of northern India
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: An Indian state's goal is social elevation of the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: The political surface hides a literal meaning: turn something over, lifting its bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something on end or upside down, so its bottom goes to the top.

clue.text: Replaced an idle CO — a half hearted type!

indicators.note: the letters are placed again in a different order

explanation.surface: A lazy commanding officer was replaced by someone lukewarm.
explanation.walkthrough: The church at Laodicea was rebuked in Revelation for being lukewarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lukewarm or indifferent, from the early church at Laodicea, chided for lack of zeal.

clue.text: Fast start has upset time Sweden previously smashed

indicators.note: previously places the scrambled country before the next piece
upset means overturned, so the letters are rearranged
smashed into pieces, the letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A rapid launch upsets the clock, after Sweden were thrashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' means a period of abstinence: Lent starts on this day. 'upset' gives ASH, 'smashed' gives WEDNES.
explanation.definitionFit: The first day of Lent, the forty days of religious abstinence.
